newsitem.title: USA: Two Coastal Oil managers indicted for stealing.
newsitem.headline: Two Coastal Oil managers indicted for stealing.

text.p: Coastal Oil New York Inc, a unit of Coastal Corp, and two of its managers have been indicted for stealing nearly one million dollars from New York City through an overbilling scheme, according to an indictment filed in the Supreme Court in Manhattan.
The two men, Samad Farooki and Joseph Colonel, and the company are charged with conspiracy, scheming to defraud and grand larceny for fraudulently inflating heating oil prices.
Coastal Oil New York, is a subsidiary of the Coastal Corp of Houston, one of the largest energy firms in the country with reported revenues of over $12 billion in 1996.

According to the indictment Coastal Oil, New York Inc (Coastal) and two of its managers are charged with intentionally and on a daily basis reporting false and highly inflated wholesale prices for heating oil to Platt's Oilgram Price Report, an oil trade publication which caused the city to overpay Coastal for heating oil supplied to facilties which included hospitals, schools, police precincts and fire houses.
"Today's indictment depicts a company that went out of its way to manipulate its wholesale prices for the sole purpose of cheating the city," Robert Morgenthau, Manhattan District Attorney said.

Lawrence Goldman, a lawyer for the New York Coastal firm said it "emphatically and uneqivocally denied all allegations of criminal misconduct by it or any of its former employees," he said in a prepared statement. The lawyer said that the company will vigorously protest the charges and "expects to be fully vindicated."
The lawyer also accused the District Attorney of hand-picking the judge, Edward McLaughlin to handle the case.
Morgenthau said that whenever someone does not like the judge, they attack the judicial selection which in this case was made by the administrative judge.
Farooki, 48, of London, England, and Joseph Colonel, 40, of New York, will be arraigned this afternoon. If convincted of the grand larceny charge the defendents face up to 15 years in state prison.

The investigation began on July 1 1992 after a competitor of Coastal complained to the city's department of finance that the prices Coastal was charging the city for heating oil "looked like phony figures."

According to court papers the price of the heating oil was determined by taking the average of the highest and lowest wholesale oil prices of certain oil companies in the city that appeared in Platt's.

The investigation revealed that from October 1992 to October 27 1993 Coastal reported false and highly-inflated heating oil prices to Platt's. As a result of this scam the city paid Coastal nearly $1 million.

"As a direct result of this scheme that these defendents are accused of engaging in, the city not only overpaid Coastal by $1 million but were forced to make overpayments to the rest of the suppliers because of the defendents scheme by artificially inflating the Platt index which was used in all the city's contracts to the tune of $3.7 million," said Kevin Ford, First Deputy Commissioner for the Department of Investigation.
